items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: I heard that broadcast. I was in Chicago and I heard that.

ctx.x: You’d hear Benny Goodman and Woody Herman, Gus Arnheim, Coon Saunders, Lunceford of course, and Basie and Andy Kirk and Ellington. I remember a great band that I heard, beside Chick Webb, Benny Carter had a band broadcasting from ballrooms here in New York City and had Eddie, what’s his name, “Canadian Sunset” had him on piano in fact.

items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: Eddie, what was the guy that played “Canadian Sunset,” had such a big hit out of “Canadian Sunset?” ... Yeah, Eddie Heywood on piano [scats]. And Eddie was flying, oh, man. I heard that broadcast. I was in Chicago and I heard that.

ctx.x: Eddie, what was the guy that played “Canadian Sunset,” had such a big hit out of “Canadian Sunset?” MR: Eddie Wood? LG: Heywood.

Heywood. Yeah, Eddie Heywood, Yes. Leslie Gourse over there. Tell her — thank you, Leslie. Yeah, Eddie Heywood on piano [scats]. And Eddie was flying, oh, man. I heard that broadcast. I was in Chicago and I heard that. And we had a man named Bob Hawk in Chicago, broadcast a thing called “Red Hot and Low Down.” And his theme was “East St. Louis Toodle-oo,” Duke’s original theme.
